regulations.title: Register your business name or corporation with the Ontario Business Registry
regulations.summary: If you're operating under any name other than your own legal name, or you've incorporated, you need to register with the Ontario Business Registry before you start selling, and corporations must file annual returns afterward.
regulations.regulation_name: Business Names Act / Business Corporations Act - Ontario Business Registry
regulations.authority: ServiceOntario / Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery
regulations.action_required: Set up an Ontario Business Registry account and register your business name, or incorporate, before selling cosmetics under that name in Ontario.
regulations.penalty_note: Operating under an unregistered business name can result in fines and difficulty enforcing contracts.
regulations.source_name: Government of Ontario - Ontario Business Registry

regulations.title: Register to collect Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) on cosmetic sales
regulations.summary: Cosmetics are taxable goods in Ontario, so once your taxable sales pass $30,000 over four consecutive calendar quarters, you need to register for a GST/HST account and charge the 13% HST.
regulations.regulation_name: Excise Tax Act - GST/HST provisions applying the Ontario HST rate
regulations.authority: Canada Revenue Agency (administers HST on behalf of Ontario)
regulations.action_required: Register for a Business Number and GST/HST account with the CRA before, or as soon as, you exceed the $30,000 small-supplier threshold.
regulations.penalty_note: Selling without required HST registration can lead to retroactive tax assessments, interest, and penalties.
regulations.source_name: Canada Revenue Agency - GST/HST for businesses

regulations.title: Register as a packaging producer under Ontario's Blue Box rules
regulations.summary: Cosmetic bottles, jars, and boxes count as packaging under Ontario's Blue Box regulation. If your business earns over $2 million a year, you must register with the Resource Productivity and Recovery Authority (RPRA) and pay for the recycling of that packaging.
regulations.regulation_name: Resource Recovery and Circular Economy Act, 2016 - O. Reg. 391/21 (Blue Box)
regulations.action_required: Check whether your revenue and packaging supply exceed the Blue Box thresholds, and if so, register with RPRA within 30 days of supplying packaged cosmetics in Ontario.
regulations.penalty_note: RPRA can pursue compliance orders and administrative penalties against producers that fail to register or report.

regulations.title: Employer Health Tax (EHT) registration once you hire staff
regulations.summary: If you hire employees to help run your cosmetics business in Ontario, you generally need to register for the Employer Health Tax, though most small employers pay nothing until their Ontario payroll passes the $1 million exemption.
regulations.action_required: Register for an EHT account with the Ontario Ministry of Finance once you begin paying Ontario remuneration, and confirm whether your payroll qualifies for the exemption.
regulations.penalty_note: Failing to register and remit EHT once payroll exceeds the exemption threshold can lead to penalties and interest.
regulations.source_name: Government of Ontario - Employer Health Tax (EHT)

regulations.title: Accessible customer service training under the AODA
regulations.summary: Any cosmetics business with at least one employee in Ontario must train staff on accessible customer service and put related policies in place, with larger businesses also needing to file periodic accessibility compliance reports.
regulations.regulation_name: Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, 2005 - Integrated Accessibility Standards
regulations.authority: Ontario Ministry for Seniors and Accessibility
regulations.action_required: Train all staff and contractors on accessible customer service, put required accessibility policies in writing, and file a compliance report if your business has 20 or more employees.
regulations.penalty_note: Non-compliance can lead to inspections and administrative penalties from the province.
regulations.source_name: Government of Ontario - Accessibility Rules for Businesses and Non-Profits
